api: Available through Azure OpenAI for direct model access, and extensible via Copilot Studio.
cons: Expensive per seat, and value varies widely by role
name: Microsoft Copilot
pros: Governance and identity continuity with existing Microsoft tenancy
Grounded in the organization's own content
Easiest enterprise procurement path for Microsoft shops
files: Works against the organization's existing Microsoft 365 content, which is the point. Standard document and spreadsheet handling.
value: Reaches into Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint with the organization's own content, under existing Microsoft tenancy, identity, and compliance controls. For most large enterprises that governance continuity matters more than raw model quality.
engine: Primarily OpenAI models running under Microsoft's enterprise infrastructure, with Microsoft's own models in some surfaces.
latency: Adequate. Perceived speed varies considerably by host application.

pricing.includes: In-app AI across Microsoft 365, tenant grounding, admin controls
Direct model access under Azure controls

quality: Model quality is competitive. The differentiator is grounding in the tenant's own data with permissions respected, not standalone reasoning.
tagline: AI embedded in Microsoft 365, where most enterprise work already happens.
use_cases: Summarising Teams meetings and long Outlook threads
Drafting and analysing directly inside Word and Excel against internal documents
Surfacing answers from SharePoint and internal knowledge under existing permissions
governance_note: Because it inherits existing Microsoft 365 permissions, it will surface anything a user already had access to. Organizations with permissive legacy SharePoint permissions frequently discover the problem only after deployment. Fix permissions before rollout, not after.
training_optout: Commercial data protection applies to licensed enterprise use: prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models. The free consumer tier operates under different terms.
